headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Continue’s filesystem/MCP access can expose Khoj-indexed notes and propagate unverified outputs into actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, while Khoj reads indexed notes/files and can ingest retrieved content. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent’s output is copied into the other’s context or shared files. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Continue reads a file or MCP result produced by Khoj and treats it as instructions
IF both agents share a workspace or note store without provenance labels
mitigations: Disable MCP tools for untrusted content paths
Separate workspaces for code and notes
Prefix retrieved text with non-instruction markers
Review any copied output before pasting between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue has broad network egress and can read/write workspace files; Khoj indexes personal notes/files and can send queries to cloud or configured search providers. If sensitive notes are placed in a shared workspace or indexed by Khoj, Continue can access them and its outputs may leave the local environment. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF sensitive notes are indexed by Khoj and also present in a shared workspace
IF Continue is allowed to read files containing personal notes or secrets
mitigations: Keep personal notes out of shared code workspaces
Restrict Continue to a narrow project folder
Disable cloud search providers in Khoj for sensitive collections
Use separate accounts or profiles for notes and coding
requires-engineering: add per-folder access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write filesystem state and shares state via filesystem across IDE windows; Khoj reads indexed documents and maintains a shared index across clients. They do not both write the same mutable store by default, but overlapping access to shared files or indexes can still cause stale reads and conflicting edits. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking warrants medium.
conditions: IF Continue writes files that Khoj also indexes or surfaces
IF multiple clients modify the same notes or workspace without locking
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Pause indexing during bulk file changes
Use separate directories for generated code and notes
Refresh Khoj index after Continue writes
requires-engineering: add file-locking or coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or file edits, and Khoj can retrieve and present those outputs as conversational context. If Khoj treats Continue’s generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect notes, summaries, or follow-on actions. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer medium rating is justified.
conditions: IF Khoj uses Continue-generated text as a source of truth without verification
IF Continue’s code or notes are copied into Khoj summaries or tasks
mitigations: Mark generated text as unverified
Require human review before acting on retrieved outputs
Keep source links alongside summaries
Use a checklist for any downstream action based on agent output

E_compliance.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, while Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents. If personal or regulated notes are indexed in Khoj and then moved into Continue-managed workspaces, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific certification mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated notes or personal data are indexed in Khoj and copied into Continue workspaces
IF either service retains logs or indexes longer than the other for the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Use separate retention settings where available
Delete stale indexed notes regularly
Avoid pasting personal notes into code buffers
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
